Variants.Content: Sambandos is located in the Norvos Highlands and the upper reaches of the Rhoyne River. Politically, it is within the hinterland under the rule of the city-state of Norvos and its bell. It is a castle mainly responsible for local garrison, tax collection and sheltering the nearby population. Walls and roads tied the surrounding population, storage, and garrison here; even if the flags were changed, this stronghold would still affect how nearby people paid taxes, traded, and sought refuge.

Entry Sambandos Keep If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

The craftsmen saw stone walls, wooden beams, iron doors, tombs and seams left by generations of repairs in Fort Sambando. The clergy guarded the bearded monks, three big bells and strict religious order. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Sambandos Keep They care about mountain roads, bells, timber, river transportation, and farms protected by the city-state. They also look at whether seeds are left after harvesting grain, and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
